user.title: Connect to Hearth
user.description: Paste the pairing token from your Hearth dashboard. The integration will open an outbound connection to Hearth; no ports need to be forwarded.

connection.title: Connection to Hearth
connection.description: Installation {installation_id} at {hub_url} is currently {status}. Turning the connection off closes the outbound link immediately; nothing can reach this Home Assistant until you turn it back on. The connection switch entity does the same. Hearth also adds five labels to Home Assistant (Hearth: tile, read only, setting, diagnostic, hide). Put them on an entity or device to choose how the Hearth app shows it; they change nothing for an AI, which still sees exactly what is exposed to Assist.

capabilities.title: What the AI may access
capabilities.description: Each switch grants the AI (your own AI client through the Hearth connector, and the Managed assistant) one area. Reads never change anything. Writes create, edit, and delete items the same way the Home Assistant editor does. Some of these let it act on your home immediately, or read more than a current state does; those are off until you turn them on. On top of all of this, only entities exposed to Assist (Settings → Voice assistants → Expose) are ever visible, and locks, alarms, cameras, and location entities are never accessible.

data.cap_entities_subscribe: Push device state as it changes (instead of waiting to be asked)
data.cap_entities_history: Read what your devices have been recording (history and statistics)
data.cap_helpers_manage: Create and change helpers (toggles, timers, counters, thresholds, template sensors)
data.cap_services_read: Read the service catalog (for authoring actions)
data.cap_devices_control: Control devices now (lights, switches, climate, covers, media, and so on)
data.cap_routines_run: Activate scenes and run scripts you already created
data.cap_integrations_manage: Add and set up new integrations (devices, services)
data.cap_areas_manage: Arrange rooms and floors, and which room each device is in
data.cap_entities_manage: Choose which devices Hearth can see
data.cap_access_control: Lock and unlock your doors from the Hearth app
data.cap_vision_view: See your cameras from the Hearth app

data_description.cap_entities_subscribe: Sends the state of entities you already exposed as soon as they change, so a light switched at the wall shows up in the app in about a second instead of up to five. It reveals nothing new — those same states were already being read every few seconds.
data_description.cap_entities_history: Lets it look up what one entity has been reading in the past — the individual readings your recorder still holds, usually the last ten days or so, and the hourly and daily minimum, maximum and average Home Assistant keeps for much longer — so it can write an automation around what actually happens here instead of guessing. One entity at a time, only entities you have exposed to Assist, never a lock, alarm, camera or location entity, and never their attributes. It is a separate switch because history says more than a current reading does: a month of it shows when the house is usually empty and when people are up.
data_description.cap_helpers_manage: Lets it make the small building blocks an automation needs — a toggle to turn a routine on and off, a timer, a counter, a schedule, or a sensor derived from ones you already have, such as a trend, a threshold, or a template. It can also rename and delete the helpers in your home. Separate from adding integrations, because that one is about connecting new devices and can ask for passwords, while this one is everyday. Deleting a helper breaks any automation that used it, and what a helper may act on or read is limited exactly as everywhere else: never a lock, alarm, camera or location entity.
data_description.cap_labels_manage: Lets it tag entities with Home Assistant labels — “holiday”, “upstairs lights” — and sort your automations, scripts and scenes into categories, so it can act on a set of things that is not a room and keep a growing list tidy. It can only label what it can already see, and Hearth's own five labels (Hearth: tile, read only, setting, diagnostic, hide), which decide how the app shows a device, are refused: those stay yours to set in Home Assistant.
data_description.cap_devices_control: Lets it act on your home as you speak, for example "turn on the kitchen lights". Locks, alarms, and cameras stay blocked.
data_description.cap_routines_run: A script does whatever you wrote in it, which may include actions Hearth itself is not allowed to perform. Enable this only if you trust your own scripts.
data_description.cap_integrations_manage: Lets it search integrations and walk through setup, filling things like IP addresses. It will never send a password, API key, or token: those steps are handed back for you to finish in Home Assistant.
data_description.cap_areas_manage: Lets the Hearth app create, rename and delete areas and floors here, change which floor an area is on, and put a device in an area — for its admins only, never for the AI. Deleting an area works as it does in Home Assistant: whatever was in it is left in no area, and automations or dashboards that named it will need updating.
data_description.cap_entities_manage: Lets the Hearth app share a device with Assist, or stop sharing it, so a newly added device can be used without coming back here. It can only offer devices Hearth is allowed to work with: locks, cameras, alarms and location entities are never listed and can never be shared. Sharing a device makes it visible to everything Hearth can do, including the assistant.
data_description.cap_access_control: Lets the Hearth app work a lock — and only the app. The AI never sees this: locks stay refused for your own AI client and the Managed assistant, and a lock written into an automation, scene or script is still rejected. Separate from device control on purpose, so turning on “act on my home” never quietly meant “open my front door”. If a lock asks for a code, set a default code on it in Home Assistant — Hearth never carries one.
data_description.cap_vision_view: Lets the Hearth app show a still picture from a camera — and only the app, only to people you have given that camera in the app. The AI never sees this: cameras stay hidden from your own AI client and the Managed assistant, and a camera written into an automation, scene or script is still rejected. Pictures are made small and sent without the camera's hidden details, such as where it is, and never as live video.

assistant.title: Assistant mode and model
assistant.description:
Hearth subscription: {tier} (active: {active}, renews {period_end}). Manage it at {dashboard_url}.

**Managed** answers inside Home Assistant Assist using the Hearth subscription. **Bring your own AI** means you talk to Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini directly and add this connector to it: {mcp_url} (see the dashboard for setup steps). **Off** removes the in-HA assistant. Model list: {models_source}.
